original_card.question: Can a legal decoder or coframe change improve the full signed moment, including changed helper targets?
methods: Construct and independently check one source-bound instance of the stated first experiment.
Seek an exact counterexample or target-specific complete-budget obstruction to that same proposed change.
original_card.acceptance_gate: A source-bound arbitrary-input identity and legal producer/consumer boundary with the complete paid and productive target invoice, including restoration, ownership, native alignment and extra charges. Price under the actual current model; historical ceiling.py assumptions must be established before use. A favorable optimistic relaxation keeps a route open but is not a completed supplier. A scoped local result remains useful; expansion requires the family-level budget gate.

first_step.inspect: Read revision 8, the selected review and live exact-source handoffs. Then follow this card's bounded first_experiment.
first_step.scope: Source-bound orientation only, not a supplier replay or theorem proof.

original_card.first_experiment: Price one complete changed itinerary with both paid and productive histograms. Check #5693/#5698 for overlap and their exact hypotheses before another coframe search. Use the signed invoice preflight where its boundary contract agrees; an inconclusive concave comparison is not a power crossing. Stop if an optimistic complete budget fails at the chosen target or native delivery remains unspecified.
original_card.bottleneck_link: Judge the actual current supplier contract and complete signed target/paid bill; frozen-profile ceilings require an applicability proof.

actual_scope: Upper bound the odd-character window of the P120 odd graph and of every nonempty subset, including the P104 port set of PR 6933. No word, moment, or kappa.
scope_change_reason: The card asks whether a decoder or coframe change improves the signed moment. This package does not change a word or a moment. It answers the odd-character half of the window question left open by PR 6933: the block-mask rank H_f is at most 36 in every characteristic other than 3, and at most 38 in characteristic 3. An odd-character mask cannot inherit the characteristic-2 window 9.
bottleneck_link: A k-block decoder mask on these ports is the fractional Haemers window of the odd graph. The characteristic-2 window is at most 9. The odd-character ceiling shows that moving the same mask to an odd field does not undercut that window; the proved patterns sit at 36 or 38. This is a scoped rank obstruction, not a supplier admission.
stop_rule: Stop after one explicit pattern whose rank is checked over Q and over F_3. Do not search for a rank-13 factorisation or a physical decoder in this package.
evidence: PROOF.md Theorems 1 and 2. verify.py prints PASS_ODD_CHAR_WINDOW rank36=36 char3_rank=38. Lower bounds 13, 14 and 15 are cited from PR 6933 Theorem 4 and are not replayed.

open_questions.question: Is w(P104; F) equal to 13 for some odd characteristic?
open_questions.why_it_matters: PR 6933 proves the lower bound 13. Equality would make the odd-character window sharp; the pattern proved here has rank 36, or 38 in characteristic 3.
open_questions.first_step: Search for one 104 by 13 factorisation over F_5 with zeros on orthogonal pairs and nonzero diagonal.
open_questions.blocked_by: The Bose-Mesner matrix 3I-A has rank exactly 36, so a sharper pattern needs edge weights outside that algebra. No such factorisation is known.

open_questions.question: Does characteristic 3 admit a 1-block pattern of rank 36 on P120?
open_questions.why_it_matters: Every other characteristic not equal to 3 has the rank-36 pattern. Characteristic 3 is the only odd characteristic where that matrix is illegal.
open_questions.first_step: Decide whether the column space of the degree-2 factorisation can be replaced by a 36-dimensional space that still solves the orthogonal equations.
open_questions.blocked_by: The degree-2 matrix constructed here has rank 38. Eight linear-only samples are inconsistent, which does not rule out a different 36-dimensional model.
